one_line_reason: All quantitative human evidence is from schizophrenia adjunct-therapy meta-analyses (pregnenolone added to antipsychotics), a clinical psychiatric population with conflicting positive/null results across studies, not the general population the catalog's generic pregnenolone products are marketed to.

selected.population: patients with schizophrenia (meta-analysis, 62 RCTs, 2914 patients pooled across multiple anti-inflammatory/adjunct agents)
selected.intervention: pregnenolone as adjunct augmentation to antipsychotic treatment, oral
selected.primary_outcome: cognitive function and psychiatric symptom scores
selected.why_selected: explicitly states cognitive improvements were significant with pregnenolone augmentation, one of the clearest positive statements in the shortlist.

selected.intervention: pregnenolone as adjunct to antipsychotic treatment, oral, among 16 agents assessed
selected.why_selected: directly states pregnenolone (along with several other agents) showed no significant effect, contradicting the positive cognitive claim elsewhere in the shortlist.

selected.population: patients with schizophrenia (quantitative review, 24 RCTs, n=1149; pregnenolone subset k=4 studies)
selected.intervention: pregnenolone augmentation of antipsychotic treatment, oral
selected.primary_outcome: total, positive, and negative symptom severity; cognition
selected.why_selected: isolates a pooled pregnenolone-only effect size (k=4 studies) and finds no overall effect, a directly quantified null result.

selected.population: patients with schizophrenia (meta-analysis, 74 RCTs, 5484 participants; most recent, bias-corrected)
selected.intervention: pregnenolone as one of several anti-inflammatory-classed adjunct agents, oral
selected.why_selected: most recent (2026) and most methodologically rigorous synthesis; reports a small positive effect size (0.20) for pregnenolone but explicitly cautions that after correcting for heterogeneity and publication bias, current evidence does not robustly support routine use.

blockers: Every shortlisted quantitative record is from schizophrenia adjunct-therapy trials where pregnenolone is combined with ongoing antipsychotic medication in a clinical psychiatric population, not the general-use context the catalog's generic pregnenolone products are sold for.

The four independent meta-analyses spanning 2015-2026 give genuinely conflicting conclusions for pregnenolone specifically: significant for cognition in one, no significant effect in two, and a small/fragile effect after bias-correction in the most recent.
No shortlisted record states an oral dose, so there is no label-mappable amount.

excluded_pmids.reason: Metabolomic profiling of follicular fluid in PCOS; pregnenolone is measured as an endogenous hormone level (found decreased), not administered as a supplement.
Systematic review of adrenocortical hormone levels in anorexia nervosa; pregnenolone is one of several endogenous hormones measured in patients, not a supplement intervention.

Metabolomic biomarker study for diagnosing acute ischemic stroke; pregnenolone sulfate is one of several endogenous circulating metabolites used as a diagnostic marker, not an administered supplement.
Plasma metabolomics in mild cognitive impairment/Alzheimer's pathology; pregnenolone sulfate is an endogenous metabolite found depleted with amyloid burden, not a supplement intervention.
Ethnopharmacology review of Notopterygium incisum, an unrelated Chinese herb; pregnenolone is not discussed as an intervention in this record.

Review of non-conventional agents for bipolar disorder; pregnenolone appears only as part of a multi-drug combination regimen (with carbamazepine, ketamine, modafinil, pramipexole) for acute bipolar depression, so its individual effect cannot be isolated.

Narrative pipeline review listing pregnenolone among 12 add-on agents said to improve cognitive function in schizophrenia; gives no quantitative effect size and is redundant with the quantitative meta-analyses already selected.

Narrative synthesis listing pregnenolone among 'positive trials' with replication in schizophrenia but provides no quantitative pooled effect size; redundant with the quantitative meta-analyses already selected.
